title: Part IX
author: David Hume
summary: Demea offers the a priori argument: everything that exists must have a cause, and the chain of causes ends in a necessarily existent Being. Cleanthes rejects it: no matter of fact can be demonstrated, and the material world itself might as well be the necessarily existent being.

notes.note: Hume's note: Dr Clarke, that is Samuel Clarke (1675–1729), whose *Demonstration of the Being and Attributes of God* (Boyle Lectures, 1704) is the source of Demea's argument.
Hume's note cites the *Nouvelles de la République des Lettres*, the monthly review edited by Pierre Bayle, for August 1685.
A transcription error: the 1779 printing has *found*.
